claims.statement: 186 orders allocated overnight are stuck in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' at east node since 06:00
claims.limitation: Alert does not attribute a cause; only observes the state and timing

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 went live at 22:00 last night with multi-node orders now reserving stock from east node first
claims.limitation: Release notes do not describe any allocation or scheduling changes; no known defects reported at time of change review

claims.statement: Every held order was flagged by the overnight allocator as a split-reservation exception
claims.limitation: Reports began at 06:00 and keep arriving; no clarification of what 'split-reservation exception' semantically means

claims.statement: Inventory allocation totals reconcile; inventory control found nothing wrong on their side
claims.limitation: Self-report from inventory control; does not rule out defects in how rule v18 splits or allocates stock

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 has a defect in how it handles multi-node stock reservation that causes orders to be marked as needing split allocation but not completing the pickup handoff
claims.limitation: Requires diagnostic inspection of what 'split-reservation exception' means and whether rule v18's logic correctly distributes stock

claims.statement: Carrier feed or pickup scheduling has a lag or failure in recognizing the east-node-prioritized allocations from rule v18
claims.limitation: Observability gap prevents seeing carrier-side confirmation; no read-only diagnostic exists yet to check carrier state

next_action.rationale: The split-reservation exception flag on all 186 held orders is the strongest signal that rule v18's multi-node reservation logic is involved. Inspecting why every order is flagged as an exception will discriminate between (a) a rule defect that creates unpickable orders, (b) normal behavior that the carrier feed is failing to process, or (c) an inventory count issue that makes stock unavailable despite reconciliation.
